title: Entropy & Gibbs free energy
examples: How does entropy affect whether a reaction can happen?
What does a negative Gibbs free energy mean for a reaction?
Can you explain the relationship between enthalpy and entropy?

explain.say: Today we are looking at Gibbs free energy changes in reactions.
The equation links three energy changes together for reactions.
A negative ΔG means the reaction is spontaneous under those conditions.
A positive ΔG suggests the reaction will not happen on its own.
The temperature determines the balance between energy and disorder.
In real life, batteries use this principle to power our devices.

faq.q: What does entropy actually measure in a reaction?
faq.a: Entropy measures the dispersal of energy or the randomness of a system. It is a measure of disorder.
asks: What is the randomness of a system?
How is disorder measured in chemistry?

faq.q: If ΔG is zero, what does that tell me about the reaction?
faq.a: A zero ΔG means the system is at equilibrium. The forward and reverse reactions occur at equal rates.
asks: What does equilibrium mean for ΔG?
When is a reaction at equilibrium?

faq.q: Does the reaction have to be exothermic for it to be spontaneous?
faq.a: No, the reaction does not have to be exothermic. Entropy can make a non-exothermic reaction spontaneous.
asks: Can a reaction release energy and still be non-spontaneous?
Is ΔH always negative for a spontaneous reaction?

faq.q: How do I use the temperature in the Gibbs equation?
faq.a: You must ensure your temperature is in Kelvin before plugging it into the equation. Remember to convert Celsius to Kelvin.
asks: What units must the temperature be in?
Do I use Celsius or Kelvin for T?

faq.q: Is Gibbs free energy an absolute property?
faq.a: Yes, ΔG is a state function, meaning it only depends on the initial and final states, not the path taken.
asks: Does the path matter for ΔG?

facts: Gibbs free energy combines enthalpy, entropy, and temperature.
A negative ΔG indicates a spontaneous process under standard conditions.
Entropy (ΔS) generally increases when a system becomes more disordered.
Temperature (T) must be used in Kelvin for these calculations.

quiz.say: A reaction has a negative ΔH and a positive ΔS. At what temperature is the reaction guaranteed to be spontaneous?
quiz.why: Since ΔH is negative and TΔS is positive, the equation becomes negative minus positive, which is always negative.

wrong.0: This assumes the entropy term will become too small to overcome the negative enthalpy.
wrong.1: This assumes the entropy term will always dominate and make the result positive.
wrong.2: Gibbs energy changes are dependent on temperature, not just one specific value.

quiz.say: If ΔG is positive, the reaction is:
quiz.why: A positive ΔG means energy must be supplied to make the reaction proceed.

wrong.0: Equilibrium occurs when ΔG is exactly zero, not when it is positive.
wrong.1: Exothermic reactions are related to ΔH, not directly to the sign of ΔG.
wrong.2: Spontaneity is determined by the overall sign of ΔG, not just the sign of ΔH.
